text:
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins became the Oilers' all-time leader in games played this week, and Edmonton gave him a standing ovation for it, NHL.com reported. The first overall pick of 2011 has spent his whole career in one sweater, and at 33 he's playing like the record should be a footnote: 11 points in 8 games since joining the lineup on Oct. 22.

The New York Times is asking what's behind the blazing start. Our answer: partly good fortune. He's shooting 25% against a range centred on 14.5%, and Edmonton has scored 5.8 more goals than its chances deserved with him on. At five on five the Oilers take 44.7% of the expected goals with him out there, below their level without him.

Seven of his 11 points came on the power play, which is also where Evolving-Hockey found most of his value last season (+8.0 goals). Eight games is a small sample, and his 4.16 points per 60 sits far above the top of his talent range (3.02). Our projection, 55 to 82 points, assumes the power play keeps humming while the five-on-five luck evens out.
headline: Nugent-Hopkins sets the record, then keeps scoring
